newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Ecopetrol, union to restart talks.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ecopetrol, union to restart talks.

text.p: Talks between Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol and the main oil workers' union USO, aimed at hammering out a new collective contract, are due to restart Tuesday, a company spokesman said Monday.
Negotiations began in January but were broken off in mid- February when USO members joined a seven-day national strike by public sector workers.
"Talks are advancing progressively. We should be restarting Tuesday," the Ecopetrol spokesman said.
The USO leadership has presented a 61-point list of demands to Ecopetrol, which it hopes will form the basis of the new two- year contract.

The most contentious demands are likely to be those for a 30 percent pay hike and for guarantees that Ecopetrol will not be divided up into core production, refining and gas operations -- which the union fears is a strong move toward privatization.
Gustavo Triana, member of the union secretariat said agreement had been reached on 24 points but declined to comment on the main hurdles to a swift accord.
"Negotiations are going on. We have not yet reached full agreement but talks are continuing," he said.

Discussions restarted after the end of the national strike but were temporarily suspended again last Tuesday when union members occupied the Cocorna field operated by U.S. company Ominex de Colombia Ltd, in the Magdalena Medio region of central Colombia.

Ominex's operating contract expired and USO workers and former Ominex employees took the action to force Ecopetrol to take direct control of the field rather than handing it over to another private sector operator.
The field produces just 600 barrels a day of difficult-to- refine heavy crude, an Ecopetrol spokesman said.
